title: Power Distribution Board Layouts
objective: Develop a repeatable approach to LV distribution-board layout decisions, balancing electrical function, maintainability, safety, interfaces and drawing clarity.

learn.heading: What senior designers should understand
bullets: Start from the circuit schedule, equipment requirements and enclosure constraints rather than drawing a layout by appearance.
Separate functional arrangement from final physical dimensions and verify vendor information before committing space.
Maintain segregation, access, cable entry, gland space, heat and maintenance considerations within the applicable design basis.
Use consistent tags and cross-references between the SLD, schedule, GA and wiring information.
Clearly identify decisions that require engineering or vendor confirmation.
learn.takeaway: A strong board layout is a coordinated design record: physical arrangement supports the electrical function and remains traceable to controlled inputs.

apply.scenario: Create a fictional 12-way LV distribution board for a small industrial facility with incomer, outgoing motor feeders, spare ways, metering and control interfaces.
tasks: Create a functional arrangement showing incomer, protection, outgoing ways, metering and spare capacity.
Prepare a preliminary GA block layout including cable-entry and maintenance considerations.
Identify at least five physical or coordination constraints that could change the arrangement.
Cross-reference each major item to a fictional circuit or equipment identifier.
Record three decisions that must be confirmed from vendor data before issue.
apply.deliverable: A sanitized preliminary board arrangement with assumptions, constraints and cross-reference notes.

questions.q: What should drive a preliminary board layout?
a: Only the visual symmetry of the enclosure.
Circuit function, protection, equipment data, cable entry, access and applicable design requirements.
questions.why: Layout is a coordinated electrical and physical design decision.

questions.q: Vendor dimensions are missing for a critical component. What is the best response?
a: Assume a standard size and issue the GA.
Show a controlled assumption if appropriate, flag the dependency and verify before final issue.
Remove the component from the drawing.
questions.why: Controlled assumptions prevent hidden design risk.

questions.q: Why are cross-references important on a board GA?
a: They make the drawing look more detailed.
They connect physical items to functional and documentary records for checking and coordination.
They eliminate the need for an SLD.
questions.why: Traceability supports multidisciplinary checking and future revisions.

check.passRule: Explain how the selected response protects coordination and maintainability.

evidence.prompt: Capture a sanitized preliminary distribution-board layout with its assumptions and coordination checks.

integration.home: Recommend Week 9 after completion and show board layout as the latest design milestone.
integration.journal: Reflect on how physical layout decisions depend on electrical function, vendor data and maintainability.
integration.portfolio: Add the sanitized board arrangement as power-distribution evidence.
